content: APBA1, also known as Amyloid beta A4 precursor protein-binding family A member 1, is a protein encoded by the APBA1 gene in humans. The protein encoded by the APBA1 gene belongs to the X11 protein family. It functions as a neuronal adaptor protein that interacts with the amyloid precursor protein (APP), which is associated with Alzheimer’s disease. This protein plays a critical role in stabilizing APP and suppressing the production of proteolytic fragments of APP, including the Aβ (amyloid beta) peptide. The Aβ peptide is known to accumulate in the brains of individuals with Alzheimer’s disease, contributing to the pathology of the condition. The product of the APBA1 gene is thought to participate in signal transduction processes. Additionally, it is considered a potential vesicular trafficking protein in the brain. It has the ability to form a complex that may link synaptic vesicle exocytosis to neuronal cell adhesion, thereby playing a role in synaptic function and communication. APBA1 has been demonstrated to interact with several proteins, including KCNJ12, CCS, CASK, and the amyloid precursor protein (APP). These interactions suggest its involvement in various cellular and molecular processes critical to neuronal function.
